correctionNotes: AutoEq/oratory1990 Harman OE 2018 correction uses a compound bass shape: low shelf @105 Hz -9.8 dB plus a very wide +18 dB peaking @81 Hz (Q0.36) and a -14.9 dB peaking @138 Hz (Q0.6) to convert the mid-bass hump into a Harman shelf. Net peak after this group is only ~4.5 dB.
Cut ~2.1 dB @1025 Hz (Q2.33) for the mild upper-bass/lower-mid dip region relative to target.
Boost ~+4.6 dB @1919 Hz (Q3.37) for the presence dip; cut -3.1 dB @2676 Hz (Q5.21) and -3.6 dB @5733 Hz (Q5.64) to tame sharp upper-mid/lower-treble.

User preference on top of Harman: +3.0 dB low shelf @40 Hz for moderate sub-bass reinforcement (seal-dependent on closed-backs).
AutoEq preamp is -4.7 dB; with the sub-bass preference shelf use about -6 dB headroom.
signature: Closed-back studio reference: deep-extending but not warm bass with a mid-bass hump around 60-100 Hz, fairly neutral lower mids, a 1-1.2 kHz dip, a 1.9-2 kHz presence lift need, and upper-mid/lower-treble energy (around 2.5-6 kHz) that can sound sharp; high treble rolls off above 10 kHz.

correctionNotes: Sub-bass is well-extended and robust; no major correction is needed below 100 Hz.

The dip around 2 kHz is a signature acoustic characteristic of Denon/Fostex wood cups. Over-correcting this region (e.g. by applying a large +6dB boost) will destroy the natural soundstage depth and introduce boxy cup reflections. Keep this upper-mid dip mostly intact, or apply only a very gentle correction (e.g., < +2dB).
Cut the sibilance/harshness peak around 5.4-5.5 kHz with a narrow bell filter (~ -4 to -6 dB, Q ~ 3.0) to remove metallic glare.
Smooth the piercing peak in the upper treble (11-13 kHz) with a high-shelf or bell filter to prevent fatiguing sibilance without sacrificing wood's airy resolution.
Avoid EQing the 8.5 kHz dip as it is likely a coupler measurement notch.
signature: Warm, spacious closed-back wood sound: robust sub-bass, relaxed upper-mids (2kHz dip), and bright treble with peaks at 5.5kHz and 11-13kHz.

The 9-10 kHz treble peak adds sparkle and air but may cause sibilance on bright recordings; a moderate cut tames this without killing the extension.
The 7 kHz dip is a typical IEM coupler feature; do not chase it with EQ.
Lower mids (300-600 Hz) are slightly pulled back relative to the bass and upper mids; a small lift can restore vocal body if needed.
signature: W-shaped single-DD tuning: well-extended, punchy bass with mid-bass emphasis; forward, emotional upper mids and vocals; smooth treble with extra sparkle near 10 kHz. Described as a 'neutral+' everyday IEM with natural coherence and musicality.
source: Bloom Audio squig.link measurement (IEC 711 clone), July 2026. Corroborated by Bloom Audio written review, Head-Fi review (Pseudonym031), and eddie0817 WordPress impressions.

signature: Closed-back studio monitor variant using YAXI PRO M-ST pads. source: AutoEq crinacle GRAS 43AG-7 Sony MDR-M1ST measured Harman correction; YAXI PRO M-ST product descriptions and community reports; user note that Yaxi pads make the sound substantially different from stock. No dedicated Yaxi-pad measurement confirmed.

correctionNotes: Mid-bass can mask lower mids; a small dip around 150–200 Hz cleans up muddiness.
Upper treble above 10 kHz is gently rolled off; a light high shelf adds air.
Default DSP already shapes the sound, so keep EQ moves modest.
signature: Consumer-warm with elevated bass and a smooth, slightly relaxed treble; mids are clean but bass can dominate at default.
source: Aggregated measurement consensus (rtings)

correctionNotes: Treat this as an open-earbud baseline: add only light bass/body support, not heavy sealed-IEM sub-bass correction.
Do not try to force extreme sub-bass; the open fit leaks low frequencies and too much low-shelf boost can erase the NH60's fast, airy character.
Keep mids mostly intact; review impressions emphasize clear, natural, warm vocals and spacious separation without muddiness.
Use a small 7-9 kHz cut when the user wants smoother treble or less metallic glare, while preserving some upper-air sparkle.
Because no measurement graph / AutoEq match was found, describe presets as estimated preference baselines rather than exact correction.
signature: Open-air/flathead earbud with clear natural mids, fast tight bass that has scale but does not truly extend like a sealed IEM, and delicate extended treble with a mild metallic brilliance that may need light glare smoothing.
source: Official/product and community sources: TimeEar NH60 official product page https://timeear.com/products/nh60-titanium-alloy-flagship-earbuds ; Flatheads news/specs https://flatheads.net/flathead-news/timeear-introduces-its-titanium-flatheads-nh60-nh80/ (14.2 mm dynamic driver, titanium alloy shell, 60 ohm / 109 dB @1 kHz, 20 Hz–20 kHz); Sekiyoxu Nishino note.com review https://note.com/sekixyo/n/n807477859dd6?hl=en (open-air earbud, tight responsive low range that does not crawl into sub-bass, clear natural mids, extended delicate treble with mild metallic brilliance). AutoEq lookup on 2026-07-06 found no exact match.

correctionNotes: Open earbud with no seal: sub-bass rolls off steeply (about -9 dB at 60 Hz and -13 dB at 40 Hz vs mids on the community graph). Support bass with a moderate low shelf plus a mid-bass bell; do not chase sealed-IEM sub-bass levels.

Requested tuning direction is a Harman-style target with appropriately enhanced bass: keep total low-end lift around +3 to +4 dB centered on 60-120 Hz so the open fit keeps its fast, clean character instead of forcing rumble.
Mids measure smooth and reviews praise natural vocals; leave 300 Hz-3 kHz essentially intact, with only a small ~280 Hz trim so the bass boost does not bleed into the low mids.
Treble falls early above ~6 kHz and sparkle is slightly subdued; a gentle 10 kHz high shelf restores some air, but avoid large upper-treble boosts because coupler behavior up there is unreliable.
Do not chase the mild 5-6.5 kHz secondary resonance or >8 kHz graph detail with narrow EQ; this is a single-unit informal measurement, so treat fine structure as approximate.
signature: Open titanium flathead earbud with smooth natural mids, fast mid-bass but rolled-off sub-bass, and relaxed detailed treble with slightly subdued sparkle; community measurement shows bass rolling off below ~150 Hz and treble falling early above ~6 kHz.
source: Head-Fi showcase review by mt877 with owner-measured L+R averaged raw FR graph (Psy smoothing, informal rig, single unit, 2026-05-09): https://www.head-fi.org/showcase/timeear-nh80-nianhua-glorious-years-earbuds.29127/reviews (graph: https://cdn.head-fi.org/a/13068385.jpg). Alias: Nianhua (Glorious Years). Specs per TimeEar/Flatheads: 14.2 mm dynamic driver, titanium alloy shell, 80 ohm, power hungry. AutoEq index lookup on 2026-07-25 found no exact match.

correctionNotes: No published measurement exists (AutoEq, squig.link, Crinacle, 0db all checked on 2026-07-29). Every band here is a review-derived preference baseline, not a correction curve - keep moves modest and do not use narrow high-Q filters.
Open fit with no seal: sub-bass leaks out. Use a low shelf around 45-60 Hz to restore weight; do not chase sealed-IEM rumble.
Unlike the NH80, mid-bass is already slightly emphasized/bloomy, so pair the sub-bass shelf with a small 150-200 Hz trim instead of a mid-bass boost.
Lower mids are reported as slightly recessed/spread out; a gentle ~400 Hz lift restores body without adding mud.
Upper mids around 2-3 kHz are already forward (the 'V' of the V shape). Do not add Harman ear-gain here; a small trim is usually the better direction.
Treble varies a lot with foam/pad choice. Use a light 5.5-7 kHz cut for metallic glare and a gentle 10 kHz shelf for the air that Korean reviewers find lacking; re-evaluate whenever the foams change.
Sits below the NH60/NH80 in refinement, so avoid heavy corrective EQ that would expose its limits - prefer a tonal-balance pass.
signature: Affordable open flathead earbud with a mild V / upper-mid-forward voicing: punchy, slightly rich mid-bass that is unusually present for an earbud but still rolls off in the sub-bass because there is no seal; lower mids sit a little back; vocals (especially female) are clear and forward; treble is extended but described anywhere from politely restrained to mildly bright and metallic depending on foam/pad. 14.2 mm dynamic driver, 44 ohm, 115 dB.
source: Community/reviewer consensus only, no measurement found (2026-07-29). Official specs: https://timeear.com/products/premium-metal-hifi-earbuds-tea-99 (14.2 mm DD, Daikoku pure-copper voice coil, 44 ohm +/-10%, 115 dB @1 kHz, 15.5 mm aluminum chamber, 3.5/4.4 mm). Reviews: arca.live/b/headphones/151248790 (KR: punchy bass, close clear vocals, treble not plentiful, pad-dependent); 0db.co.kr/REVIEW_USER/6056497 (KR owner: fun balance, good bass for open type, more resolving than FiiO FF1); bisonicr.ldblog.jp/archives/56047269 (JP: upper-mid-focused mild V, bright extended highs, mid-bass bloom); zhuanlan.zhihu.com/p/698398864 (CN: restrained, natural mid-highs); note.com/sekixyo/n/nc5946b966801 (JP: tight fast bass, smooth treble, follows NH60 direction with less refinement). AutoEq/squig.link lookups on 2026-07-29 found no match.

correctionNotes: Use the leather-pad measured correction as the primary baseline for Simon's current pad setup; Kuulokenurkka AutoEq has a dedicated 'Yamaha YH-5000SE (leather earpads)' result.

Chord Alto drive headroom should not be the bottleneck, but digital headroom still matters because the correction uses large +8 dB bass and +7 dB upper-presence boosts; keep a negative preamp around -7.5 dB for X8.
Reduce the 1.3 kHz excess substantially to avoid honk/forwardness, then restore the 2.6–4 kHz presence recession carefully for Crinacle/Harman-like clarity without making the headphone shouty.

Treat >7 kHz cautiously: pad seal, ear position, and measurement rig variance are large, so use only the measured broad shelf/limited resonance shaping rather than chasing narrow ultra-treble notches.
signature: Open-back orthodynamic/planar flagship. Leather-pad measurements show a large bass/sub-bass deficit relative to Harman/Crinacle-style over-ear targets, a strong 1.2–1.4 kHz forward/honk region, recessed 2.5–4 kHz presence/attack, and fit/fixture-sensitive treble above ~7 kHz.
source: Primary for current setup: AutoEq Kuulokenurkka measured leather-pad result, Yamaha YH-5000SE (leather earpads), https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jaakkopasanen/AutoEq/master/results/Kuulokenurkka/over-ear/Yamaha%20YH-5000SE%20%28leather%20earpads%29/Yamaha%20YH-5000SE%20%28leather%20earpads%29%20ParametricEQ.txt .
